display.purpose: Document title field at the head of the sheet; 27px at 860px and below.

headline.purpose: Prose h1 at 30px; h2 25px and h3 21px share the setting. Regular weight.

body.purpose: Manuscript prose on a 620px measure, 20px paragraph space; 18px at 860px and below.

stamp.purpose: Story-time stamp in the masthead, uppercase serif.

apparatus.purpose: Rail rows, tabs, controls and notices (Source Sans 3 400-500).

gloss.purpose: Gloss note bodies; emphasis lifts to ink, not bold.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked labels (0.1-0.12em): rail sections, margin cues, note heads, AI caption.

key.purpose: Raised note key letter after a noted phrase, out of flow.

shadows.name: drawer
shadows.purpose: The open rail drawer overlaying the page at 1180px and below. The only shadow.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one ease, for every fade and draw.

motion.name: fade
motion.purpose: Opacity: cues, keys, gloss notes, tab close, rail drawer. 0ms under reduced motion.

motion.name: draw
motion.purpose: Background size of layer marks and leader tick stroke, drawn left to right. 0ms under reduced motion.

motion.name: arriving
motion.purpose: AI caption while a segment is generating; disabled under reduced motion.

breakpoints.name: wide-gloss
breakpoints.purpose: At and below: margin 80px, gutter 32px, gloss 220-300px.

breakpoints.name: rail-drawer
breakpoints.purpose: At and below: rail becomes a fading overlay drawer with a masthead toggle.

breakpoints.name: single-column
breakpoints.purpose: At and below: one column, wrapped masthead, cues above paragraphs, gloss as a keyed list after the prose.

narrative.overview:
A late-printed edition of the writer's own manuscript, read by lamplight. The page is a warm near-black ground with bone ink in three steps and hairline rules; the prose sits in a single serif column at book measure, and everything the world knows about it (who speaks, when it is, what is implied, which names are canon) is set around it as apparatus: margin cues to the left, a lettered gloss to the right, marks painted behind the words. The prose is the stage; the apparatus is quiet, small, sans-serif, and attached to the words it is about.

Density is that of an annotated edition, not a dashboard. Chrome is a rail, a masthead and hairlines; there are no panels, no cards around notes, and no chat surface. AI work is always visible and signed but never loud: the one saturated warm colour in the system belongs to AI-made text and nothing else.

Layers are paint, not layout. Every mark is in the DOM all the time; turning a layer on changes only colour, background size and opacity, so the prose never moves (measured 0 px of movement, click to paint within 34 ms in the shipped build). Motion follows the same grammar: marks fade, underlines draw left to right, nothing slides or bounces.
keyCharacteristics: Warm near-black ground, bone ink in three steps, 1px hairline rules for all structure.
Old Standard TT for the writer's words and the page's stamps; Source Sans 3 for every piece of apparatus.
Vermilion reserved for the double-ruled AI segment plate.
Each layer hue does one job: speaker tints, time blue, subtext gold.
Gloss notes are lettered keys on gutter ticks, never cards.
Paint-only layers: colour, background size and opacity; never box geometry.
Fade 140 ms, draw 150 ms, one expo-out ease; reduced motion zeroes both.

rules.name: The Vermilion Signature Rule
rules.body: Vermilion marks AI-made text and only AI-made text: the plate's two rules and its caption. If a surface is not an AI segment, it carries no vermilion, not even as an accent or an error.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Each layer hue means one thing everywhere it appears. Blue is always story time, gold is always subtext, a speaker tint is always that speaker in that scene. A new feature that needs colour takes a neutral, not a layer hue.

rules.name: The Paired Tint Rule
rules.body: A speaker tint never appears alone: it is always paired with the speaker's name, in the margin cue or the rail swatch row, so colour is never the only carrier of who is speaking.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: The writer's words and the edition's stamps are serif; everything the app says is sans. Never set apparatus in Old Standard or prose in Source Sans; the writer's inline `[[ notes ]]` are the deliberate crossover, always italic sans at 15px, because they are the writer talking to themselves.

rules.name: The Fixed Weight Rule
rules.body: Weight, size and style never depend on a layer. World entities are always 700 and notes always italic apparatus whether or not their layer is on, because changing them would reflow the line.

rules.name: The Paint-Only Rule
rules.body: A layer may change colour, background size and opacity. It may never change a box: no width, padding, margin, border, font weight, display or position. Any new layer rule is tested by toggling it and measuring zero prose movement.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn, not lifted: borders are 1px in `rule`, strengthening to `rule-strong` on hover. The pressed-toggle underline is an inset 2px line, not elevation.

dos: Do keep every layer mark in the DOM and switch it with `data-layer-*` attributes on the sheet, changing only colour, background size and opacity.
Do reserve vermilion (#e34b2f) for the AI segment plate and its caption.
Do give each layer hue exactly one meaning, and pair every speaker tint with the speaker's name.
Do set the writer's prose in Old Standard TT at 19px / 1.62 on a 620px measure, and all apparatus in Source Sans 3.
Do attach notes to their words with a key letter and a gutter tick, and resolve them with one-click text actions.
Do fade opacity in 140 ms and draw underlines and ticks left to right in 150 ms on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`, and zero both under reduced motion.
Do draw structure with 1px hairlines (`rule`, `rule-strong`) and tonal steps.
donts: Don't let a layer change weight, size, padding, border, display or position; it reflows the prose.
Don't put gloss notes in cards, boxes or filled panels; they are keyed text in the margin.
Don't slide, bounce or translate anything, including the narrow-screen rail drawer.
Don't use vermilion for errors, emphasis or brand; errors use raised umber with bone ink.
Don't reuse a layer hue for an unrelated meaning.
Don't add shadows beyond the overlay rail drawer.
